official.deadline_note: VU's advised Master's programme application deadline for scholarship applicants is 1 December 2026 - you must already be conditionally admitted before you can apply for the VUFP, and an admission decision can take up to about 6 weeks. VU also advises submitting even earlier if the programme's admission procedure includes an intake or assessment.
official.status_note: VU publishes the 2027/2028 VUFP round with 'Applications are welcome from November 1st 2026' and 'Deadline VUFP application: 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET)'. Registration for the Master's programme itself is already possible from 1 October 2026, and the 2027-2028 VUFP-NLS application form is published on the page.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The official page states: 'The VUFP scholarship covers the tuition fees only. It does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances. Be aware that you must be able to finance these living expenses by yourself.' The Terms and Conditions repeat this: 'The VUFP scholarship covers tuition fees only.' VU does not state a single euro figure for the award; the amount waived equals the programme's non-EEA institutional tuition fee, which VU publishes per programme - for 2027-2028 the non-EEA institutional Master's rates run from EUR 6,500 to EUR 39,120 per year (for example EUR 25,370 for most School of Business and Economics and Faculty of Law programmes, EUR 24,970 for most Faculty of Science programmes, EUR 39,120 for M Medicine).
benefits: The VUFP scholarship covers the tuition fees only. It does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances.
When applying for the VUFP scholarship, you automatically apply for the NL Scholarship (formerly HSP) as well. No separate application is necessary.

NL Scholarship is a one time contribution towards the costs of living of EUR 5,000 for the entire duration of your study period (the VUFP Terms and Conditions PDF for 27-28 states 'EUR 5,000 EUR or EUR 10,000'); awarded only for the first year, with around 20-25 available per year.
VU Amsterdam has committed to providing approximately 1 million euros towards attracting highly motivated and excellent students.
As one of our most excellent students, you agree to become an international student ambassador during your studies at VU Amsterdam.

One VUFP scholarship will be reserved for an applicant who previously completed a semester or full academic year abroad at VU Amsterdam via the Semester in Amsterdam programme and who is now applying for a full-time Master's programme.
eligibility: You hold a non-EU/EEA passport and you are not eligible for the lower tuition fee; you do not have the Dutch nationality.
You can prove your academic excellence (GPA equivalent to a Dutch 8).

You are conditionally or unconditionally admitted to the first year of a full-time English-taught Master's programme at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam starting per September 2027; students starting in February cannot apply.
Joint programmes where VU Amsterdam does not administer the admission process are excluded from VUFP.

The degree with which you are seeking admission has not been obtained in the Netherlands, you do not have a degree from an education institution in the Netherlands, and you are not currently enrolled in a Bachelor or Master programme in the Netherlands.

You do not need to complete a preparatory programme before the start of your Master. Students already enrolled in a two-year Master's programme who have not been awarded the VUFP scholarship in 2026/2027 are not eligible to apply for the VUFP scholarship for 2027/2028.
requirements: Fill out the VUFP-NLS application form for academic year 2027-2028 - older versions of the application form will not be accepted.
At the end of the form, paste the GPA proof / programme transcript and a grading scale explanation with a clear explanation of the GPA calculation.
Save it as one file in .PDF format and upload it in the Scholarship section of your personal VU dashboard on vu.nl (located on the Complete Registration page).

To be considered complete, the application form must include all the answers and the GPA proof / programme transcript; not answering one or more questions or not including the GPA proof will result in your application being considered incomplete and therefore not evaluated.
You can apply for the VUFP only for one Master's programme, and you can submit your application only once - you will not be allowed to submit it again.

You do not need to convert your grades to the Dutch ones; the VUFP Scholarship Committee decides on the local grade equivalents for the Dutch grade of an 8.0, and even if you have already completed a Master's degree VU looks only at your GPA from your bachelor's degree.
documents: Completed VUFP-NLS application form for academic year 2027-2028, saved as a single PDF
Bachelor's programme transcript or GPA proof (most up-to-date grades if not yet graduated)
Grading scale explanation showing how the GPA is calculated, with a clear explanation of the GPA calculation
selection_criteria: All VUFP applications received by 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET) will be reviewed by the faculty of the applied for Master's programme.
Faculties nominate applicants to the Central Scholarship Committee, which awards scholarships to the most talented students.
The results will be based on the academic performance and motivation.

The total score used to rank all applicants is based on several factors, of which GPA is only one - other factors such as motivation for this university/specific programme, future ambitions and extracurricular activities also play a significant part.
Meeting the minimum GPA requirement is only a minimum and is by no means a guarantee to actually be offered the VUFP scholarship.
VU does not assess scores sent by email in advance of the application period - you must submit your complete application to be evaluated.
coverage: The VUFP scholarship covers the tuition fees only.
It does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances.

Through the same single application you are automatically also considered for the NL Scholarship, a one time contribution towards the costs of living of EUR 5,000 for the entire duration of your study period, awarded only for the first year - around 20-25 are available per year and only a few of the VUFP awardees will get the NL Scholarship.
application_method: Step 1 (from 1 October 2026): Register for a Master's programme in Studielink and complete it in your personal dashboard on vu.nl. You must have been conditionally admitted to the Master's programme before you can apply for the VUFP. Advised deadline Master's programme application: 1 December 2026.

Step 2 (from 1 November 2026): Submit your VUFP application in your personal VU dashboard by filling out the VUFP-NLS application form, pasting the GPA proof / programme transcript and grading scale explanation at the end, saving it as one PDF and uploading it in the Scholarship section of your personal dashboard.
Step 3: Decision - the Central VUFP Committee decides which students will be offered a VUFP scholarship.
Step 4: Results - all students receive an e-mail/notification. Expected date: mid-March 2027 (6 weeks after the deadline).

Step 5: Acceptance - selected candidates accept/decline the VUFP and NL Scholarship offer in their personal VU dashboard. Deadline to accept: end of March 2027 (2 weeks after the results have been published).
official.application_route: Register in Studielink plus the personal VU dashboard, obtain at least conditional admission, then upload a single completed 2027-2028 VUFP-NLS PDF to the Scholarship section of the personal VU dashboard - there is no separate scholarship portal and no e-mail route.
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EU/EEA passport required and not eligible for the lower (statutory) tuition fee; Dutch nationality excluded. VU notes 8 residence permit types that make a student pay the statutory tuition fee instead of the institutional fee (types I-V, Article 50 TEU, and EU/EEA and EU/EEA family-member types).
official.international_eligibility: Yes - non-EU/EEA international students only; EU/EEA students and Dutch nationals are not eligible for the VUFP
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all full-time English-taught Master's programmes at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam starting September 2027; joint programmes where VU Amsterdam does not administer the admission process are excluded. No field-of-study or agency restriction is published.
official.duration: One- or two-year full-time English-taught Master's programme starting September 2027. The scholarship will only be extended for the second year of a two-year Master's programme if 100% of the ECTS during the first year have been achieved.
official.description: The VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) offers talented prospective non-EU/EEA students the unique opportunity to pursue a Master's degree at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam as a merit-based tuition fee waiver. VU states the scholarship covers the tuition fees only and provides no additional allowance towards study or living costs, so applicants must be able to finance living expenses themselves. Applying for the VUFP automatically also enters the applicant for the NL Scholarship.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee waiver for non-EU/EEA students
official.english_requirement: The VUFP page itself publishes no test score - the requirement is admission to the full-time English-taught Master's programme. VU's published Master's English proficiency requirement is programme-specific: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 for most programmes (no minimum subscore for many, 6.0 minimum subscores for others such as Accounting and Control, Business Administration and Information Sciences) and 7.0 for a few (e.g. Marketing, Law, International Crimes Conflict and Criminology), or TOEFL iBT 92 on the old scale / 4.5 on the new scale from 21 January 2026 onwards. Tests must be no more than two years old by 1 September of the start year; exemptions apply for degrees fully taught in English in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK, the USA, Singapore, South Africa or the EU/EEA. The VU TOEFL ITP costs EUR 150 and is not accepted for non-EU/EEA students who need a study visa.

not_confirmed: number of VUFP scholarships awarded per year
verification.notes: VU publishes no per-student monetary figure for the VUFP: the award waives the programme-specific non-EEA institutional tuition fee, which VU publishes separately (2027-2028 range EUR 6,500-39,120 per year), and the only monetary figure on the scholarship page is the total programme commitment of approximately EUR 1 million. Amount, currency and period are therefore recorded as null rather than guessed. The brief's official_source_url (vu.nl/en/deducation/scholarships/vu-fellowship-programme) returns HTTP 404 - the live VUFP content now sits on the incoming Master's scholarships page, which was used as the primary source and is cited above. English test scores are programme-specific and published by VU on separate official PDFs, not on the scholarship page. The VUFP Terms and Conditions PDF for 2027-28 was downloaded and read in full; it confirms tuition-only coverage, no deferral, and the ambassador obligation. VU publishes 'approximately' EUR 1 million committed to the programme overall, which is a budget total and not an individual award value.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a tuition-only award: the money stops at your fee invoice, so Amsterdam rent, food, health insurance, visa and flights stay entirely on you - the EUR 5,000 NL Scholarship you are automatically entered for is a living-cost contribution for the first year only, it goes to roughly 20-25 people a year, and VUFP holders are not guaranteed it. The application itself is deceptively simple: one PDF, one programme choice, one submission, and a single unanswered question makes the file incomplete and unevaluated rather than merely scored lower. The real gate is sequencing - you must already hold at least conditional admission, and VU warns an admission decision can take about six weeks, so anyone who starts in January has effectively missed the round. Treat the 1 December 2026 advised programme deadline, not the 1 February scholarship deadline, as your actual deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants whose bachelor's GPA already sits at the Dutch 8 equivalent, who can write a specific motivation for one programme, and who have family support or a loan that can absorb two years of Amsterdam living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Start the Studielink application for exactly one English-taught Master's in October 2026; VU's scholarship-track advised deadline is 1 December 2026 and an early start matters if the programme has an intake or assessment.
Get an English bachelor's transcript plus an official grading-scale explanation ready to paste into the form - VU does its own conversion to the Dutch 8 equivalent, so do not pre-convert.
Download only the current 'Application form 2027-2028' from the VU scholarship page; older versions are rejected outright.
Confirm you actually pay the institutional rate - some non-EU/EEA passport holders qualify for the statutory tuition fee through their residence permit type and are therefore ineligible.
Budget the EUR 100 non-refundable VU application fee for international degree holders, plus the tuition payment you would owe by 31 August 2027 if you are admitted but not awarded.
Plan the visa/residence permit in parallel: the general non-EU/EEA Master's application deadline is 1 April 2027 and enrolment must be complete by 31 August 2027.
Check your English test date against the two-year validity rule measured from 1 September 2027, and book early if a retake may be needed.
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete form - one unanswered question or a missing GPA proof/transcript means the application is not evaluated at all, not just marked down.
Assuming 8/10, 80% or 16/20 automatically equals a Dutch 8; VU converts by grade distribution statistics and only a small share of foreign grades reach the threshold.
Applying for admission to several Master's and leaving the programme choice unresolved - you must nominate exactly one programme for the VUFP.
Missing the advised 1 December 2026 programme deadline and therefore lacking conditional admission when the committee scores files on 1 February 2027.
Being an existing two-year Master's student who missed the VUFP in 2026/2027 - you cannot reapply for 2027/2028, so plan self-funding for year two.
Dropping below 100% of first-year ECTS on a two-year programme, which silently cancels the second year of the waiver.
Treating the automatic NL Scholarship entry as a safety net; only a few VUFP awardees get it and it never covers year two.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except tuition: Amsterdam rent, food, health insurance, the visa/residence permit, flights, study materials and the EUR 100 application fee. VU states explicitly that the VUFP provides no allowance towards rent, food or insurance. The optional EUR 5,000 NL Scholarship is a first-year living-cost contribution for about 20-25 people a year and is not a travel or tuition grant.
document_audit: The transcript and grading-scale explanation must be pasted inside the application form and saved as one single PDF - separate uploads are not accepted.
Use the 2027-2028 form version only; VU will not accept older versions.
If you have not yet graduated, submit the transcript with your most up-to-date grades rather than waiting for the diploma.
Only your bachelor's GPA counts - a completed Master's is explicitly ignored for VUFP scoring.
If your bachelor's was taught in English but the transcript does not say so, obtain a stamped and signed statement from your university or you will be pushed to a language test.
Keep the conditional admission email - it is checked before your scholarship file is scored, and it is also what unlocks the accommodation and visa services in your dashboard.
alerts: One submission only - no resubmission and no revision after you press submit.
February 2027 starters are excluded; only September 2027 entry qualifies for this round.
A scholarship granted for one academic year cannot be postponed to another academic year, and the Terms and Conditions state deferral of scholarships is not possible.
Changing programme after an award is only considered in exceptional cases and only within six weeks of the original programme's start date.
If you take no action within two weeks of the results email, the offer is withdrawn.
Report any change of nationality or any interruption to the International Office immediately in writing - nationality changes are a listed condition of the award.
One VUFP slot is reserved for Semester in Amsterdam alumni; if that is you, follow the standard procedure and then notify the Semester in Amsterdam team that you applied.
As an awardee you commit to acting as a VU international student ambassador for the whole Master's, including a kick-off session in October.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in Studielink and complete the VU dashboard application, obtain at least conditional admission, then upload one completed 2027-2028 VUFP-NLS PDF with transcript and grading scale appended to the Scholarship section of your personal VU dashboard before 1 February 2027 23:59 CET; the faculty reviews and nominates, the Central Scholarship Committee awards, results are emailed mid-March 2027, and you accept or decline in the dashboard by end of March 2027.
